title: Unify engineering handoffs and reviewable test outcomes
scope: Repair shared stage contracts, bounded serialization, phase timing, safe failed-test review and rejected-objective continuation across existing engineering task profiles.
riskAnalysis: Server-authored version selection changes new request/schema contracts while immutable historical contexts replay unchanged. Failed test assertions become review evidence only after existing isolation, source integrity and shutdown checks. This grants no new model tools, repository publication, independent acceptance or customer access.

threatModel.assets: Exact source/task/workspace identities, provider credential isolation, historical request hashes, immutable receipts, test isolation and shutdown evidence.
threatModel.trustBoundaries: Chief receipt to model schema and backend validator; untrusted test output to typed review evidence; runtime version to historical replay; provider byte stream to counted and parsed response.
threatModel.abuseCases: Forged or missing runtime marker, cross-workspace count proof, stale source, oversized response, failed tests relabeled passed, fake cleanup, omitted QA findings, fabricated acceptance, repeated consumed authority.
threatModel.mitigations: Exact runtime comparisons, closed known marker, shared finite byte policy, authenticated request-bound token counts, unchanged source validators, native result/manifest hashes and independent cleanup checks. Final reporting preserves QA/Auditor disagreement.

rollback: Revert the shared runtime change on the feature branch and return its alias to the qualified nonpaid1301433 Preview. Keep all historical and new receipts unchanged. No Production operation.

negativePaths.malformed-response: Rich and malformed schema fixtures, over-limit byte/token input, forged source and invalid expressions remain denied.
negativePaths.stale-state: Current runtime/source/plan bindings and historical request-hash regressions preserve exact replay while unknown marker is denied.
negativePaths.concurrency: Existing controller CAS, cumulative sequence and one-time grant tests remain; no parallel provider dispatch or new retry is introduced.
negativePaths.cancellation: Real controller cancellation and independently fired phase timers verify original operation deadline and revoked authority.
negativePaths.worker-interruption: Existing restricted child and test-provider interruption fixtures preserve failure receipts, usage and cleanup status.
negativePaths.api-outage: Provider error, partial response and persistence failures remain denied with typed sanitized evidence.
negativePaths.authorization-denial: Unknown or dropped marker, stale approval, foreign workspace, forged count proof and missing cleanup remain denied.
negativePaths.spending-limit: Current owner-approved monitor-only financial policy is preserved; historical receipts and uncertainty remain. No inference or new spending authority is supplied by this change.
negativePaths.partial-execution: Safe failed assertions reach technical review only after bound complete results and confirmed shutdown; infrastructure or unconfirmed cleanup still stop.

proactiveReview.architecture: Reuse the existing organization, activation controller, journal, provider adapter and restricted data/test workers. New shared modules replace duplicated contract decisions; no competing orchestration.
proactiveReview.dependencies: No new package, provider, credential or dependency installation. Existing pinned parser and isolated test image remain unchanged.
proactiveReview.threats: Review marker cannot grant authority; unknown marker fails. Byte increases do not alter actual token limits. Failed test results cannot become backend technical success.
proactiveReview.failureModes: Historical missing output remains unknowable. New malformed/oversized/forged responses fail with preserved diagnostics; cleanup uncertainty remains unresolved rather than invented.
proactiveReview.faultInjection: Cases include partial/refused/malformed responses, bad source, forged count provenance, canceled model and test phases, result binding, persistence and stop failures.
